facts.statement: The genus Jeholornis was described by Zhou and Zhang in 2002.
facts.quote: authority: Zhou & Zhang, 2002

facts.statement: Fossils of Jeholornis were first found in the Jiufotang Formation in Hebei Province, China.
facts.quote: Fossil Jeholornis were first discovered in the Jiufotang Formation in Hebei Province, China

facts.statement: Jeholornis had long tails, few small teeth, and a body size comparable to turkeys.
facts.quote: Jeholornis had long tails and few small teeth, and were approximately the size of turkeys

facts.statement: Jeholornis ate seeds from cycads, Ginkgo, or similar plants.
facts.quote: Their diet included seeds of cycads, Ginkgo or similar plants

facts.statement: Adult Jeholornis reached a maximum length of 75 cm (2.5 ft) and weighed between 2.27 and 9.1 kg (5–20 lbs).
facts.quote: maximum adult length of up to 75 cm (2.5 ft) and an estimated weight of 2.27-9.1 kg (5-20 lbs)

facts.statement: The species J. prima had no teeth in the upper jaw and only three small teeth in the lower jaw.
facts.quote: Jeholornis prima lacked teeth in their upper jaws, and had only three small teeth in their lower jaws

facts.statement: The teeth of all Jeholornis species were small, blunt, peg-like, and lacked serrations.
facts.quote: The teeth in all three species were small, blunt and peg-like with no serrations

facts.statement: Jeholornis had robust arms that were longer than their legs, indicating strong wing muscles.
facts.quote: Their arms were robust and longer than the legs, with relatively well-developed shoulder girdles indicating strong wing musculature

facts.statement: The hallux (first toe) of Jeholornis was only partially reversed, unlike the fully reversed toe seen in modern birds.
facts.quote: The first toe, or hallux, which is reversed in modern birds and used to perch in trees, was only partially reversed in both Jeholornis species

facts.statement: A 2009 study by Gregory M. Erickson found that Jeholornis had a slow rate of growth compared to most modern birds.
facts.quote: A study by Gregory M. Erickson in 2009 has shown that Jeholornis (along with Archaeopteryx) had relatively slow ontogenic development

facts.statement: Researchers speculate that Jeholornis may have had a metabolism similar to modern kiwi birds due to their slow growth rate.
facts.quote: it has been speculated that Jeholornis could have had a metabolism similar to these

facts.statement: Flight feathers found in Jeholornis were asymmetrical and aerodynamic, reaching lengths of up to 21 centimeters.
facts.quote: The first specimen shows that the flight feathers were asymmetrical (and therefore aerodynamic, as in modern flying birds) and up to 21 centimeters long

facts.statement: Because Jeholornis tail feathers did not overlap, the tail was likely used for display rather than flight.
facts.quote: The tail feathers did not overlap, and so could not have formed a lift-generating surface, so the tail was probably used mainly for display

facts.statement: The species J. palmapenis possessed 11 tail feathers arranged like a palm frond.
facts.quote: In at least one species, Jeholornis palmapenis, there were 11 tail feathers

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Jeholornis is J. prima.
facts.quote: type_species: Jeholornis prima

facts.statement: Zhou and Zhang classified Jeholornis as the type genus of the family Jeholornithidae and the order Jeholornithiformes.
facts.quote: Zhonghe Zhou and Fucheng Zhang classified Jeholornis in a new family, Jeholornithidae, of which it is the type genus, and the order Jeholornithiformes

facts.statement: More than 100 Jeholornis fossils have been discovered, but only seven have been formally described.
facts.quote: Over 100 specimens of Jeholornis have been found, though only seven have been formally described

facts.statement: A specimen reported in 2013 contained preserved structures interpreted as ovaries.
facts.quote: A sixth specimen, STM2-51, was reported in 2013 and preserved round structures in the body cavity which were interpreted as ovaries

facts.statement: It is debated whether the genus Jixiangornis is a synonym of Jeholornis, as a 2014 analysis suggested it might belong to short-tailed avialans instead.
facts.quote: However, a phylogenetic analysis performed in 2014 found that it may actually be more closely related to short-tailed avialans (Pygostylia) than to Jeholornis

facts.statement: A 2020 study concluded that Shenzhouraptor is a valid species distinct from Jeholornis prima, rejecting earlier suggestions that they were synonymous.
facts.quote: In 2020, a publication of a new genus and species of jeholornithiform, Kompsornis longicaudus, by Wang and colleagues included a re-evaluation of the diagnostic characteristics of all Jeholornis species, including the holotype of Shenzhouraptor. This examination concluded that Shenzhouraptor was a valid species distinct from Jeholornis prima and other jeholornithiforms, rejecting the suggestion that they are synonymous.

facts.statement: Jeholornis lived approximately 120 million years ago during the Early Cretaceous (Aptian stage) in what is now China.
facts.quote: Jeholornis es un género de ave primitiva que vivió en el Cretácico Inferior (hace aproximadamente 120millones de años, en el Aptiense), en lo que hoy es China.

facts.statement: Adult Jeholornis reached a length of approximately 80 centimeters.
facts.quote: Jeholornis es una de las mayores aves mesozoicas, con una longitud de aproximadamente 80cm en ejemplares adultos.

facts.statement: The skull of Jeholornis was short, high, and curved downward.
facts.quote: El cráneo era corto y alto, curvado hacia abajo.

facts.statement: The forelimbs of Jeholornis were longer than the hindlimbs and possessed strong wing musculature.
facts.quote: Las extremidades superiores eran más largas que las inferiores, y presentaban una fuerte musculatura alar.

facts.statement: The first toe (hallux) of Jeholornis was reversed like in modern birds and featured curved claws.
facts.quote: El primer dedo, el hallux, estaba revertido, de manera similar al de las aves modernas, y presentaba garras curvas.

facts.statement: The wing feathers of Jeholornis were asymmetrical, aerodynamic, and approximately 21 centimeters long.
facts.quote: Las plumas de las alas eran asimétricas (y por lo tanto aerodinámicas, como en las aves modernas) y largas, de 21cm aproximadamente.

facts.statement: The tail of Jeholornis ended in a fan of feathers extended only at the tip, similar to Microraptor but unlike Archaeopteryx.
facts.quote: La cola de Jeholornis acababa en un abanico de plumas, extendido solamente en el extremo de la cola (como en Microraptor y no como Archaeopteryx).

facts.statement: One specimen of Jeholornis was fossilized with gastroliths in its stomach.
facts.quote: In 2017 it was announced, that one specimen was fossilized with gastroliths in its stomach.

facts.statement: A 2022 study identified Jeholornis prima as the earliest known fruit-eating bird.
facts.quote: A 2022 study by the University of Oxford, england and Linyi University showed that Jeholornis prima was the earliest known fruit eating bird.

facts.statement: Research indicates that Jeholornis consumed the entire fruit, not just the seeds.
facts.quote: During this study, they also found that Jeholornis was not just eating the seeds but the entire fruit itself.

facts.statement: The ability to eat fruits likely developed when plants began developing new kinds of fruits around 135 million years ago.
facts.quote: This trait possibly developed when plants somewhere around 135 million years ago started developing new kinds of fruits.

facts.statement: A co-evolutionary relationship between birds like Jeholornis and fruit-producing plants started about 120 million years ago.
facts.quote: Some birds like Jeholornis evolved the ability to eat the fruits and a co-evolutionary relationship started about 120 million years ago.

facts.statement: Primitive avialans like Jeholornis could not achieve true flapping flight but were capable of semi-powered gliding or parachuting.
facts.quote: Primitive avialans like Archaeopteryx, Confuciusornis, and Jeholornis would not have been able to lift their arms vertically to achieve true flapping flight, though semi-powered gliding or parachuting would have been possible.

facts.statement: Examination of claw curvature suggests Jeholornis may have been able to perch and spent much of its time in trees.
facts.quote: Examination of the claw curvature in Jeholornis suggests it may have been able to perch and may have been at least partly arboreal, spending much of its time in trees.

facts.statement: It is debated whether the reversed appearance of the hallux in Jeholornis is a true anatomical feature or an artifact of fossil crushing.
facts.quote: Jeholornis was initially described as having a reversed hallux, though others cast doubt on this interpretation, noting that the reversed appearance could be an artifact of the way the fossils were crushed.

facts.statement: The genus Jeholornis was established by Zhou & Zhang in 2002.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Zhou & Zhang, 2002

facts.statement: The species J. palmapenis was described by O'Connor et al. in 2012.
facts.quote: subdivision: J. prima Zhou & Zhang, 2002 J. palmapenis (O'Connor et al., 2012)

facts.statement: Shenzhouraptor and Jixiangornis are listed as synonyms of Jeholornis.
facts.quote: synonyms: Shenzhouraptor Zhou & F. C. Zhang, 2002 Jixiangornis Ji, Ji & Zhang, 2002

facts.statement: The genus Jeholornis includes at least two species: J. prima, named for its primitive tail appearance, and J. palmapenis, named for tail feathers arranged like palm leaves.
facts.quote: El género Jeholornis contiene al menos dos especies: Jeholornis prima, descrita en 2002, llamada así por la apariencia primitiva de su cola, y Jeholornis palmapenis, descrita en 2012, llamada así por las plumas de su cola, cuya disposición recuerda a las hojas de una palmera.

facts.statement: Jeholornis belongs to the family Jeholornithidae and the order Jeholornithiformes, where it is the only representative.
facts.quote: Jeholornis se incluye dentro de la familia Jeholornithidae y en el orden Jeholornithiformes, dentro de los cuales es el único representante.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of J. prima, cataloged as IVPP V13274, was described in 2002 and is held at the Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology in Beijing.
facts.quote: El holotipo, de la especie J. prima, llamado IVPP V13274, se encuentra en la colección del Instituto de Paleontología de vertebrados y Paleoantropología de Pekín, y fue descrito en 2002.

facts.statement: Five specimens of Jeholornis have been formally described.
facts.quote: Se han descrito formalmente 5 especímenes de Jeholornis.

facts.statement: It remains unknown whether Jeholornis and Shenzhouraptor represent the same genus or two distinct ones.
facts.quote: no se sabe si realmente son el mismo género o dos diferentes

facts.statement: Jeholornis was a herbivorous bird, and seeds measuring 8-10mm were found in the crop region of one fossil.
facts.quote: Jeholornis era un ave herbívora, y en uno de sus fósiles se encontraron semillas en la zona del buche de 8-10mm de tamaño.

facts.statement: Juvenile specimens possessed more teeth than adults, suggesting they lost them as they matured.
facts.quote: Otros especímenes encontrados, clasificados como ejemplares juveniles, poseían más dientes, aunque se indica que al madurar los perderían.

facts.statement: Its small size and head shape suggest a specialized diet of seeds.
facts.quote: Su reducido tamaño, junto con la forma de la cabeza del animal, sugieren una dieta especializada en semillas.

facts.statement: Like Archaeopteryx and other primitive birds, Jeholornis could not raise its forelimbs above its body due to the arrangement of its shoulder bones.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, al igual que éste, Confuciusornis y otras aves primitivas, la disposición de los huesos del hombro indica que el animal no podía elevar sus extremidades superiores por encima del cuerpo.

facts.statement: The curvature of its claws indicates that Jeholornis was at least partially arboreal.
facts.quote: La curvatura de las garras señala que Jeholornis era un animal de hábitos arbóreos, al menos parcialmente.

facts.statement: The presence of a reversed hallux, similar to modern birds, supports the hypothesis of an arboreal lifestyle.
facts.quote: Una de las adaptaciones que apoyan la hipótesis es la presencia del hallux revertido, como en las aves modernas.

facts.statement: Jeholornis lived during the Barremian to Aptian stages, between 125.77 and 113.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Barremian to Aptian (125.77 to 113.2 million years ago)
